newsitem.title: USA: Crop drying demand spurs on U.S. spot propane late.
newsitem.headline: Crop drying demand spurs on U.S. spot propane late.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices were higher in late trade on Thursday, driven up largely by crop drying demand in the Midwest, players said.
"The market should be coming off, but it's staying up because people are really pulling hard on propane in Conway," said one Houston trader.
Prices plunged this morning on bearish inventory data released late yesterday, but then quickly began to bounce back up.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, spot propane rose a quarter cent in late trade to between 53.00 cents and 53.25 cents a gallon. This morning it traded at 51.75 cents.
In Conway, Kansas, hub spot propane, which fell to 52.00 cents this morning, worked its way back up to 53.75/54.00 in late trade.
"Corn drying is really going well right now, especially in the North," said one Midwest trader.
Propane is used as fuel to dry corn crops before they are brought to the market or stored.
Other liquid gases were reported quiet in late activity. Belvieu ethane purity was valued at 32.75/33.00 cents and Conway ethane at 29.50 cents, players said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
